title: Star trails
summary: Stack many 30 s frames into circling stars.

media.alt: Star trails circling the celestial pole above an observatory

blocks.note: 120 frames of 30 s is an hour of trails. Longer = longer arcs.

steps: Moonless, clear night away from towns. Point at **Polaris** (north) for circles; any other direction gives arcs.
Frame a strong foreground: a tree, a rock, a building.
Manual focus on a bright star, then tape the ring. Turn off lens IS and long-exposure noise reduction.
M mode: f/2.8, ISO 800, 30 s. Take one test frame and check the foreground isn't black.
Set the interval timer just longer than the shutter (about 32 s) and the number of shots to unlimited.
Leave it for an hour or more. Then stack the frames with StarStaX (computer) or a phone app.

items: Noise reduction must be off, or the camera leaves a gap after every frame and the trails break up.
One single long exposure (15–60 min in Bulb) works too, but the sky glow and noise build up.
Shoot a few frames at the start with the lights of a passing car or a torch to light the foreground.

steps: Switch to **MF** and focus on a bright star in magnified live view.
Lens IS off on the tripod: the R10 has no in-body stabiliser, so the lens switch is the one that matters.
**Shooting 5 › Long exp. noise reduction: Disable** so there's no gap between frames.
**Shooting 7 › Interval timer › Enable**. Interval **00:00:32**, shots **00** (runs until you stop it).
Press the shutter fully to start. Press it again to stop.
Copy the frames to a computer and stack them in StarStaX (free) or Sequator.
canon-r10.note: A shot is skipped if the shutter is longer than the interval, so keep the interval a couple of seconds over 30 s.
